Senses.Explanation: The records use this transitive appraisal for seeing through a saying, case, person, condition, or position before or after it is presented. Literally, 'look through' or 'look and break through.' The compound occurs 509 times in 154 allowed texts. It is used transitively of a saying, case, person, condition, or distinction; in passive clauses someone or something is 'seen through.' Hongzhi asks, 'What is the eye with which you can see through it?'. Comments on earlier cases say that someone saw through Lingyun and Mahakasyapa, that Tianning saw through Dahui, or that an interlocutor should see through an action before it occurs. The passive form appears in a warning about being seen through by someone at a later time (他時異日被人覷破). The fuller form 'be able to see through' occurs 40 times in 25 texts, while the emphatic 'with one look, see through' (一覷覷破) occurs 19 times in 17. The texts do not supply a separate technical definition beyond these observable objects, contrasts, questions, and active/passive constructions.
Senses.Note: The two hits for 'one who sees through this' use the final graph as the pronoun 'this,' not as a definition formula. They were therefore not treated as self-definitions. The corpus range is grammatical rather than polysemous: the same verb occurs with people, words, cases, and named distinctions as its object.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正當十五日。覷破兩頭。直得君臣道合。父子氣和。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (宏智禪師廣錄). Extensive Record of Hongzhi, end-of-summer assembly address. Hongzhi uses the verb of seeing through the two ends. The exact headword-bearing actor is Hongzhi Zhengjue.
